summary:
The headline today isn't a hot streak — it's the complete absence of one. Every rating's 14-day and 7-day windows are flatlined at 0-0 (n=0), meaning the model's recent-form signal is dead silent heading into November 27th. That's unusual this deep into a 144-date sample and it means RJ should lean on season-long baselines and the thin-but-perfect 30-day strong-play results rather than chase any "hot category" narrative, because none exists right now. All four ratings show the same 30-day line: 1-0 at 100%, R2 the biggest single-game winner at +3.0u, R1/R3/R4 each +2.0u — encouraging, but n=1 across the board, so treat it as a tiebreaker, not a thesis.

With trend data dry, the slate decision today should be built off the category-combo agreement table, which hasn't drifted: trends+sp remains the strongest dual signal at 58.0% (370-268, n=638), trends+runs close behind at 57.3% (404-301, n=705). Any pick where trends and SP ratings line up together deserves the highest confidence tag on tonight's board. Where ratings disagree, fall back to the team-when-liked data — if LAD or BOS show up as the model's side tonight, that's where the real edge sits: LAD strong-plays are 28-7 (80%, +27.0u) and BOS strong-plays are 22-7 (76%, +19.0u), both well clear of the field. MIL and TBR also clear 69-70% straight and strong, so a LAD-MIL or BOS-TBR matchup type lean should be bet with size if it appears. Fade NYY on anything beyond a baseline flag — strong-play backing is 9-14 (39%, -4.0u), the only team leader bleeding units, and bullpen_fatigue remains the weak link across every rating (R1 47%, R4 45% season), so don't let a NYY/fatigue-driven angle talk RJ into a play tonight.
